question: Find the gain percentage, given that Anubha sold her scooter for ₹31524 gaining (1)/(6) th of the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of the scooter be 6 units.

Since the gain is 1/6 of the SP, Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of the scooter = ₹31524

Gain = 1/6 of SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88ba9a8c367da53d3d20dbb08ee8da89c7f19da7bb436134a43852c5cb0218cf.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gain = (1 ÷ 6) × 31524

⇒ Gain = ₹5254

⇒ CP = 31524 − 5254 = ₹26270

⇒ Gain % = (5254 ÷ 26270) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit/Loss Calculated on Selling Price

When profit is erroneously calculated as a percentage of Selling Price (SP), actual Profit % on CP = [Profit% on SP ÷ (100 − Profit% on SP)] × 100.

Basic Rules of Profit and Loss

Profit or loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless a question specifies that it is calculated on the Selling Price.

Relation between SP, CP and Profit

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 + Gain %) ÷ 100]
